newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FUND-RELATED BUYING TO BOOST BELGIAN SHARES.
newsitem.headline: FUND-RELATED BUYING TO BOOST BELGIAN SHARES.

text.p: The Bel-20 share index, which set its 25th record high so far this year on Tuesday, can rise further in coming weeks on investor hedging of fund purchases, dealers said.
"We expect the market to go higher, driven by liquidity, institutional investor and private investor buying click funds," said analyst Stefan Casteleyn at brokerage Colyn & Co.
The Bel-20 closed up 0.71 percent at 2,220.77, with a strong 3.03 billion Belgian francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
One trader said Kredietbank and Generale Bank had started launching click funds on Monday, spurring the blue-chip index higher today.
"We won't see any correction as long as click funds are being launched on the market, unless there's a major correction in the U.S.," said another trader.
Traders said financial institutions would continue to launch click funds, which lock in profits at certain Bel-20 index levels, until the ex-dividend period started in May.
"There are no sellers now because what would they do with the cash they make," said analyst Casteleyn.
Attention centred on banks, the main bourse gainers, fuelled by speculation of a possible merger between Generale Bank and BBL .

"We have a stand-alone policy for now, but we are receptive to the message that a bigger Belgian bank would be a good thing," Generale Bank chief Ferdinand Chaffart told a news conference on the bank's 1996 earnings.
Generale Bank closed up 1.8 percent at 14,000 francs, with its holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) ending up 1.7 percent at 2,930 francs.
BBL closed up 1.1 percent at 8,290 francs. Rival Kredietbank gained ground, up 1.71 percent at 13,350 francs.
Elsewhere, cement maker CBR climbed 1.76 percent to 3,460 francs, fuelled by expectations of strong 1996 results, due out this week, and good growth in 1997.
One trader said investors welcomed CBR's international expansion policy. CBR, a unit of Germany's Heidelberger Zement, has recently picked up stakes in companies in Turkey, eastern Europe and China.
